title: The popular version. Skype was a Microsoft product.
description:
Skype was a Microsoft product. It launched in 2003, from Niklas Zennstrom and Janus Friis. Microsoft bought it in 2011.

The Estonian developers credited with creating the software. The first public beta came out on 29 August.

It copied the peer to peer design of Kazaa. Friis and Annus are credited with proposing it as a way to cut the cost of voice calls.

Connected users Microsoft cited for 2010, in the release announcing an $8.5 billion cash deal.

Microsoft retired Skype on 5 May 2025. Users moved to the free version of Teams. Skype's user base had fallen to about 36 million by 2023.

Four Estonians built it. A blog post ended it.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skype (read): founded 2003 by Niklas Zennstrom and Janus Friis; software credited to Estonian developers Ahti Heinla, Priit Kasesalu, Jaan Tallinn and Toivo Annus; Friis and Annus credited with proposing a Kazaa style peer to peer design to cut voice call costs; first public beta 29 August 2003; Microsoft deal announced 10 May 2011; retired 5 May 2025; about 36 million daily users in February 2023.
- https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000789019/000119312511134416/dex991.htm (read): Microsoft's press release, 10 May 2011: $8.5 billion in cash, and "170 million connected users and over 207 billion minutes of voice and video conversations in 2010".
- https://www.techrepublic.com/article/microsoft-skype-shutting-down/ (read): Microsoft confirmed the retirement in a blog post on 28 February, Skype closes on 5 May 2025, users move to Teams Free, and the user base had dwindled to 36 million by 2023.
